slots.claim_sentence: The Shigella flexneri effector protein OspI suppresses the human inflammatory response by deamidating the enzyme UBC13 at position Q100.
slots.clarification_sentence: Shigella flexneri is a pathogen that causes severe diarrhea by invading the intestine and hiding from the immune system.

slots.claim_sentence: Deamidation of UBC13 inhibits the synthesis of K63-linked polyubiquitin chains, which prevents the activation of the NF-κB immune signaling pathway.
slots.clarification_sentence: Normally, UBC13 and TRAF6 must bind to trigger chemical signals that call for immune cells to clear the infection.

slots.claim_sentence: Deamidation of the protein UBC13 inhibits its interaction with the protein TRAF6RING.
slots.clarification_sentence: The bacterial modification specifically targets the binding interface where the two proteins usually meet.

slots.claim_sentence: The deamidation of UBC13 at Q100 creates a new intramolecular salt-bridge that competes with a critical intermolecular salt-bridge at the UBC13/TRAF6 interface.
slots.clarification_sentence: A salt-bridge is an electrical attraction between a positive and negative part of a protein.

slots.claim_sentence: Electrostatic repulsion between the negatively charged glutamate (E100) and the TRAF6 RING surface prevents necessary transient interactions.
slots.clarification_sentence: Because both the modified site on UBC13 and the surface of TRAF6 are now negatively charged, they push each other away.

slots.claim_sentence: The bacterial effector OspI from Shigella flexneri inhibits host immune responses by modifying transient protein-protein associations and using salt-bridge competition.
slots.clarification_sentence: This study shows how a tiny chemical change can have a massive effect on how proteins find and stick to each other during an infection.

slots.claim_sentence: Working memory depends on the coordinated interaction of distributed brain networks.
slots.clarification_sentence: Working memory is the ability to hold and manipulate information in the mind over short periods.

slots.claim_sentence: Brain regions may exchange information by synchronizing their rhythmic electrical activity.
slots.clarification_sentence: These rhythmic waves occur when many brain cells send signals at the same time.

slots.claim_sentence: Researchers used transcranial alternating current stimulation (tACS) to manipulate brain waves in healthy volunteers.
slots.clarification_sentence: The researchers applied 6 Hz stimulation to the right frontoparietal network of the brain.

slots.claim_sentence: The frontoparietal network involves regions at the front and side of the brain that support memory.
slots.clarification_sentence: Stimulation targeted the middle frontal gyrus and inferior parietal lobule.

slots.claim_sentence: Synchronous stimulation improved reaction times during difficult memory tasks.
slots.clarification_sentence: This improvement occurred during the 2-back task but not the easier 1-back task.

slots.claim_sentence: Participants had to monitor number sequences and spot repeated patterns.
Brain scans showed that synchronous stimulation increased activity in the parietal region.
slots.clarification_sentence: Increased activity in the right inferior parietal lobe led to faster responses.

slots.claim_sentence: The parietal lobe is a part of the brain involved in processing sensory information and spatial reasoning.
The timing of the electrical stimulation changed how different parts of the network communicated.
slots.clarification_sentence: This stimulation increased functional connectivity between the parietal and frontal areas.

slots.claim_sentence: Functional connectivity measures how well different brain areas work together.
The study provides evidence that synchronization across large networks drives cognitive performance.
slots.clarification_sentence: The results show a direct link between brain synchronization and working memory performance.

slots.claim_sentence: The granular retrosplenial cortex is essential for both spatial and non-spatial behaviors.
slots.clarification_sentence: These behaviors include navigation, learning, and memory.

slots.claim_sentence: Researchers used optogenetic mapping in mice to study the granular retrosplenial cortex.
slots.clarification_sentence: This region contains low-rheobase neurons and regular-spiking neurons.

slots.claim_sentence: The anterior thalamus and dorsal subiculum provide spatial information to low-rheobase neurons.
slots.clarification_sentence: Low-rheobase neurons are specialized to receive compass-like signals about where an animal is facing.

slots.claim_sentence: Regular-spiking cells process non-spatial information from the claustrum and anterior cingulate.
slots.clarification_sentence: Regular-spiking cells handle data from different brain regions while their neighbors handle space.

slots.claim_sentence: Parallel processing is enabled by precise anatomical organization within layer 1.
slots.clarification_sentence: The physical layout of the brain wiring ensures that the two types of information do not get mixed up.

slots.claim_sentence: Low-rheobase neurons can compute the speed of head rotation.
slots.clarification_sentence: Low-rheobase cells calculate how fast the mouse is turning even when incoming signals only say which way the mouse is facing.

slots.claim_sentence: Low-rheobase neurons are the primary subtype for encoding spatial information.
slots.clarification_sentence: This discovery identifies a specific cell type that is likely responsible for the ability to stay oriented in space.

slots.claim_sentence: The granular retrosplenial cortex is critical for knowing where a person is and how to get to a destination.
slots.clarification_sentence: Damage to the retrosplenial cortex causes spatial disorientation similar to symptoms seen in Alzheimer’s disease.

slots.claim_sentence: Precise axonal and dendritic arborization within layer 1 permits this parallel processing.

slots.claim_sentence: Stable flower shapes are important for reproductive success and attracting pollinators.
slots.clarification_sentence: Petals are usually required to open the flower and help attract pollinators.

slots.claim_sentence: Petal number is invariant in Arabidopsis thaliana flowers.
slots.clarification_sentence: These flowers consistently produce four petals.

slots.claim_sentence: Cardamine hirsuta exhibits variable petal numbers ranging from zero to four.
slots.clarification_sentence: This species can display a variable number of petals on a single plant.

slots.claim_sentence: Divergence in the floral regulator APETALA1 accounts for the difference in petal number robustness.
slots.clarification_sentence: This gene is also known as AP1.

slots.claim_sentence: Arabidopsis thaliana AP1 confers robustness by masking the effects of quantitative trait loci.
slots.clarification_sentence: These quantitative trait loci are also called QTL.

slots.claim_sentence: The Cardamine hirsuta version of the AP1 gene fails to complement this function.
slots.clarification_sentence: Differences in regulatory regions contribute to this divergence.

slots.claim_sentence: Variable petal number is maintained in Cardamine hirsuta despite standing genetic variation.
slots.clarification_sentence: Natural populations have enough variation to produce four-petalled flowers.

slots.claim_sentence: The AP1 gene in Arabidopsis thaliana hides the expression of other genetic traits.
slots.clarification_sentence: This masking ensures the plant consistently grows four petals.

slots.claim_sentence: The divergence mapped to upstream regulatory rather than coding regions.
slots.clarification_sentence: The Cardamine hirsuta AP1 gene does not provide the same stability.

slots.claim_sentence: Arabidopsis thaliana is a common research model that maintains flower shape despite genetic differences.
slots.clarification_sentence: Invariant floral forms are robust to natural perturbations.

slots.claim_sentence: The AP1 gene acts like a buffer to hide genetic variations.
slots.clarification_sentence: Masking prevents other genes from changing the petal count.

slots.claim_sentence: Researchers used laser-capture microdissection to isolate and profile genes in the Schmidtea mediterranea intestine.
slots.clarification_sentence: Schmidtea mediterranea is a flatworm that can regenerate its entire digestive system after injury.

slots.claim_sentence: The study identified over 1,800 intestine-enriched transcripts using this sensitive bulk tissue method.
slots.clarification_sentence: This approach found 809 transcripts that previous single-cell studies did not detect because laser-capture microdissection allows researchers to focus on specific bulk tissue sections.

slots.claim_sentence: The planarian intestine performs consolidated roles that humans split among several different organs.
slots.clarification_sentence: These roles include functions typically handled by the human liver and small intestine, such as energy storage and nutrient absorption.

slots.claim_sentence: The study found regionalization of gene activity between the medial and lateral intestinal domains.
slots.clarification_sentence: This spatial specialization is particularly evident in cells called goblet cells, which are organized into distinct zones within the digestive tract.

slots.claim_sentence: The gene gli-1 is required for goblet cells to undergo regeneration after injury.
slots.clarification_sentence: A second gene called RREB2 is needed for the maintenance of these cells, acting as a transcription factor that turns other genes on or off.

slots.claim_sentence: This genetic atlas provides a resource for investigating how the digestive system repairs itself.
slots.clarification_sentence: These findings support comparative analyses to understand human gastrointestinal pathologies by generating new insights into cellular processes that are often dysregulated in disease.

slots.claim_sentence: Understanding how simple animals like planarians regrow their gut could eventually help treat human conditions like acid reflux or surgical damage.

slots.claim_sentence: Mitochondria require mechanisms to recognize and remove misfolded proteins to maintain essential functions.
slots.clarification_sentence: Mitochondria are essential to cellular bioenergetics and metabolism.

slots.claim_sentence: Quality control pathways for misfolded mitochondrial proteins are currently poorly defined.
slots.clarification_sentence: A universal Mitochondria-Associated Degradation pathway for mitochondrial outer membrane proteins has not been described.

slots.claim_sentence: Researchers established temperature-sensitive mitochondrial outer membrane proteins as model substrates in yeast.
slots.clarification_sentence: The researchers used the yeast Saccharomyces cerevisiae for these experiments.

slots.claim_sentence: The model proteins are degraded from the mitochondrial outer membrane by the ubiquitin-proteasome system.
slots.clarification_sentence: The proteins remain on the mitochondria when the proteasome is not working.

slots.claim_sentence: Ubiquitination of the substrates is mediated by the ubiquitin ligases Ubr1 and San1.
slots.clarification_sentence: San1 and Ubr1 normally handle misfolded proteins in the cytosol and nucleus.

slots.claim_sentence: Mitochondria-associated degradation of misfolded proteins requires the SSA family of Hsp70 chaperones.
slots.clarification_sentence: The Hsp40 chaperone Sis1 is also required for this process.

slots.claim_sentence: Degradation involves the Cdc48-Npl4-Ufd1 AAA-ATPase complex and the transmembrane adaptor Ubx2.
slots.clarification_sentence: Ubx2 has a discrete and functional pool located at the mitochondria.

slots.claim_sentence: The study identifies a unique quality control pathway using both cytosolic and mitochondrial factors.
slots.clarification_sentence: This pathway is distinct from endoplasmic reticulum-associated degradation.

slots.claim_sentence: The SSA1 chaperone is specifically required for the ubiquitination step of these mitochondrial substrates.
slots.clarification_sentence: Sis1 slowed the turnover of both model proteins used in the study.

slots.claim_sentence: Ubiquitinated mitochondrial quality control substrates require the Cdc48-Npl4-Ufd1 complex for efficient proteasomal degradation.
slots.clarification_sentence: The protein Doa1 is also implicated in the degradation of these substrates.

slots.claim_sentence: Ross River virus is a significant mosquito-borne pathogen in Australia and the Pacific Islands.
slots.clarification_sentence: Researchers built a mechanistic model to understand how temperature drives this virus. This virus infects 2,000 to 9,000 people each year and can cause long-term joint pain. Because mosquitoes cannot control their body temperature, their ability to spread diseases depends on the temperature of their environment.

slots.claim_sentence: Transmission of the Ross River virus peaks at a moderate temperature of 26.4°C.
slots.clarification_sentence: This specific middle temperature allows the virus to spread most effectively. The relationship between temperature and transmission is not a straight line. There is a specific middle temperature where the virus spreads most effectively.

slots.claim_sentence: Ross River virus transmission stops at thermal limits of 17.0°C and 31.5°C.
slots.clarification_sentence: The disease cannot spread if the environment is too cold or too hot. Biological traits of the mosquitoes and the virus prevent the disease from spreading at these extremes.

slots.claim_sentence: The virus is endemic year-round in tropics but seasonal in temperate areas.
slots.clarification_sentence: Low temperatures in temperate regions force transmission to zero for part of the year. In the tropics, temperatures stay within the transmission range all year. Cooler areas experience winter temperatures that drop below the virus limit.

slots.claim_sentence: Climate warming will increase transmission in temperate areas but decrease it in tropical areas.
slots.clarification_sentence: Warming may push tropical temperatures above the upper thermal limit for the virus. Tropical areas are already near the ideal temperature. Further warming will make them too hot for the virus. Warming in cooler areas will bring them closer to the ideal range.

slots.claim_sentence: Nonlinear models are essential for predicting disease responses to climate change.
slots.clarification_sentence: These models account for specific temperature limits rather than assuming a simple increase. Traditional models might assume that more heat always means more disease. This study shows that the hump-shaped response to temperature is critical for accurate planning.

slots.claim_sentence: The specific behavioral correlates of motor cortical beta oscillations remain unresolved in neuroscience.
slots.clarification_sentence: Beta oscillations are brain waves that emerge when individuals are paying attention or waiting.

slots.claim_sentence: Researchers recorded motor cortex activity while three macaques performed a novel neurofeedback task.
slots.clarification_sentence: The researchers used electrodes to monitor brain activity as the monkeys learned tasks.

slots.claim_sentence: The monkeys volitionally brought their beta oscillatory power to an instructed state before reaching.
slots.clarification_sentence: The monkeys controlled a cursor on a screen using only their brain activity.

slots.claim_sentence: Trials with high beta power resulted in slower movement onset times during arm reaches.
slots.clarification_sentence: Reaches preceded by a reduction in beta power exhibited significantly faster movement onset times.

slots.claim_sentence: Population neural activity shifts farther from a movement onset state during beta oscillations.
slots.clarification_sentence: High beta power moves the neural state further from the threshold required for movement.

slots.claim_sentence: This study establishes a neural basis for slowed movement onset following beta oscillatory activity.
slots.clarification_sentence: The generation of beta oscillations favors a state that compromises readiness for upcoming movements.

slots.claim_sentence: Motor cortical beta oscillations have been reported for decades without a clear behavioral function.
slots.clarification_sentence: Understanding these oscillations might reveal how they contribute to symptoms of Parkinson’s disease.

slots.claim_sentence: The monkeys were trained to perform a sequential beta neurofeedback arm-reaching task.
slots.clarification_sentence: This method allowed researchers to link population neural activity to specific behaviors.

slots.claim_sentence: Distances to the movement onset threshold are greatest when the brain reaches a high beta target.
slots.clarification_sentence: The brain's collective neural activity moves into a state that is mathematically distant from the state needed to trigger a movement.

slots.claim_sentence: The brain uses these waves to pause the motor system which makes it harder to start moving quickly.
slots.clarification_sentence: Beta oscillations favor a low-risk state that ensures the animal remains still.

slots.claim_sentence: Some viruses like Marburg and Dengue activate and benefit from the Nrf2 protein to help them infect cells.
slots.clarification_sentence: Nrf2 is a protein that normally helps cells turn on anti-oxidant genes to protect themselves.

slots.claim_sentence: Sulforaphane is a natural compound found in cruciferous vegetables that can activate the Nrf2 protein.
slots.clarification_sentence: Sulforaphane is produced in cruciferous vegetables after they are damaged or chewed.

slots.claim_sentence: Sulforaphane treatment stops HIV from infecting macrophages but it does not work in T cells.
slots.clarification_sentence: Macrophages and T cells are both types of white blood cells that HIV targets.

slots.claim_sentence: When Nrf2 levels are lowered, HIV infects macrophages more easily and Sulforaphane becomes less effective.
slots.clarification_sentence: Researchers used a technique called siRNA to specifically reduce the amount of Nrf2 in the cells.

slots.claim_sentence: The ability of Sulforaphane to fight HIV depends on its ability to activate and move the Nrf2 protein.
slots.clarification_sentence: This confirms that the drug works by triggering the cell's own internal defense system.

slots.claim_sentence: Sulforaphane blocks infection after entry but before formation of 2-LTR circles.
slots.clarification_sentence: 2-LTR circles are markers that show the virus has reached the cell nucleus.

slots.claim_sentence: This anti-viral effect does not use the common defense proteins SAMHD1 or MX2 that usually stop HIV.
slots.clarification_sentence: This suggests Nrf2 uses a previously unknown pathway to block the virus.

slots.claim_sentence: This discovery shows that HIV can be blocked by Nrf2 activation in a novel way.
slots.clarification_sentence: This provides a potential new strategy for HIV treatment by triggering the body's own antioxidant response.

slots.claim_sentence: Aedes-borne arboviruses like dengue and Zika cause increasing morbidity and mortality worldwide.
slots.clarification_sentence: Arboviruses are viruses transmitted to humans by mosquitoes such as Aedes mosquitoes.

slots.claim_sentence: A Zika outbreak in the Dominican Republic allowed researchers to compare transmission drivers.
slots.clarification_sentence: This outbreak followed a large dengue epidemic in the same region.

slots.claim_sentence: About 75% of dengue cases occurred in people aged <20 years.
slots.clarification_sentence: Zika infections were more widely dispersed across different age groups in the population.

slots.claim_sentence: Reported Zika infections were highly clustered among females at 73.8% of cases.

slots.claim_sentence: Guillain-Barre syndrome attack rates were slightly higher in males than in females.
slots.clarification_sentence: Guillain-Barre syndrome is a serious neurological condition sometimes triggered by the Zika virus.

slots.claim_sentence: Existing dengue immunity had little impact on the reported attack rates of Zika.
slots.clarification_sentence: Prior exposure to dengue did not seem to change the risk of Zika infection.

slots.claim_sentence: Awareness campaigns likely drove increased health seeking behaviour among women of reproductive age.
slots.clarification_sentence: This behaviour explains why more Zika cases were reported in women than in men.

slots.claim_sentence: Media campaigns and screening are recommended for women of reproductive age during outbreaks.
slots.clarification_sentence: These strategies help identify cases in groups at higher risk for specific complications.

slots.claim_sentence: Fluctuations in hetR expression in nearby cells are coupled across two to three cells.
slots.clarification_sentence: This coupling sets the spatial scale for how individual cells interact along the filament.

slots.claim_sentence: These correlations arise primarily from intercellular molecular transfer rather than cell division.
slots.clarification_sentence: Cells communicate by passing molecules through channels instead of just inheriting traits during division.

slots.claim_sentence: Fluctuations after nitrogen deprivation build up on those present under nitrogen-replete conditions.
slots.clarification_sentence: Random variations in gene activity exist even when nitrogen is plentiful for the cells.

slots.claim_sentence: The inhibitor PatS, communication via SepJ, and HetR auto-regulation determine these expression fluctuations.
slots.clarification_sentence: PatS acts as a brake while HetR reinforces its own production through auto-regulation.

slots.claim_sentence: The study highlights differences between inhibitors PatS and HetN and septal proteins SepJ and FraC/FraD.
slots.clarification_sentence: Different proteins manage communication and inhibition depending on the level of nitrogen availability.

slots.claim_sentence: Stochasticity and communication combine to control the one-dimensional developmental pattern in Anabaena.

slots.clarification_sentence: Learning slows down when participants must manage more shape-mapping associations at once.

slots.claim_sentence: Many countries lack the baseline data necessary to plan and launch public health programs for neglected tropical diseases.
slots.clarification_sentence: Neglected tropical diseases cause significant physical debilitation and lowered economic productivity, but programs cannot start without data.

slots.claim_sentence: Researchers developed the Integrated Threshold Mapping methodology to simultaneously map four specific neglected tropical diseases.
slots.clarification_sentence: The protocol targets lymphatic filariasis, trachoma, schistosomiasis, and soil-transmitted helminths.

slots.claim_sentence: The ITM protocol determines if a disease has reached the threshold for intervention rather than providing exact prevalence figures.
slots.clarification_sentence: A country must prove a disease has passed a specific threshold established by the World Health Organization before starting treatment.

slots.claim_sentence: The study compared the Integrated Threshold Mapping methodology with standard WHO methodologies in one district each in Mali and Senegal.
slots.clarification_sentence: Researchers compared both methodologies in terms of feasibility, cost, time, and human resource needs.

slots.claim_sentence: The ITM methodology reached the same conclusions as standard WHO methods for trachoma, lymphatic filariasis, and soil-transmitted helminths.
slots.clarification_sentence: The new methodology resulted in more targeted intervention recommendations for schistosomiasis by using the sub-district as the measurement unit.

slots.claim_sentence: The ITM methodology was found to be practical, feasible, and more cost-effective than standard mapping methods.
slots.clarification_sentence: The methodology resulted in a 31% cost saving in Mali and a 19% saving in Senegal by using resources more efficiently.

slots.claim_sentence: The Integrated Threshold Mapping tool could help endemic countries implement necessary public health programs more easily.

slots.claim_sentence: Organ aging is associated with reduced stem cell occupancy in the niche.
slots.clarification_sentence: The niche is a specialized environment that houses and supports stem cells.

slots.claim_sentence: Notch signaling increases with age in Drosophila female germline stem cells.
slots.clarification_sentence: This increased signaling results in the removal of stem cells from the niche.

slots.claim_sentence: Notch signaling regulates the adhesion of germline stem cells to the niche.
slots.clarification_sentence: The pathway alters adhesion by changing the expression of the protein E-cadherin.

slots.claim_sentence: The age-dependent increase of Notch signaling is partially mediated by Sex lethal.
slots.clarification_sentence: A reduction in the protein Sex lethal helps drive this signaling change.

slots.claim_sentence: BMP signaling levels remain unaffected in stem cells with defective Notch signaling.
slots.clarification_sentence: BMP signaling is a separate pathway that promotes the self-renewal of stem cells.

slots.claim_sentence: Notch signaling in the niche cells decreases as the organism ages.
slots.clarification_sentence: This reduction in the niche contrasts with the increase seen in stem cells.

slots.claim_sentence: These findings regarding Notch and adhesion may be relevant to metastatic cancer.
slots.clarification_sentence: In metastatic cancer cells, Notch signaling is also known to suppress cell adhesion.

slots.claim_sentence: Notch signaling in the niche cells is necessary to maintain niche integrity.
slots.clarification_sentence: The reduction of signaling in these cells helps explain how aging disrupts the stem cell environment.

slots.claim_sentence: Elimination of Sex lethal in germline stem cells elevates Notch signaling.
slots.clarification_sentence: This elevation of signaling triggers early loss of the stem cells from their environment.

slots.claim_sentence: HIV infection currently cannot be cured but can be controlled using combinations of multiple anti-retroviral drugs.
slots.clarification_sentence: These anti-retroviral drugs work together to keep the virus at low levels in the body.

slots.claim_sentence: Because HIV genotypes vary between individual patients, it is difficult to determine which drug combination will provide effective treatment.
slots.clarification_sentence: Each patient carries a unique version of the virus that may respond differently to specific medications.

slots.claim_sentence: Existing HIV treatment models are typically based only on viral sequence data and do not account for the chemical similarity of drugs.
slots.clarification_sentence: These models ignore how the physical structure of a drug affects its ability to stop the virus.

slots.claim_sentence: Researchers applied proteochemometric models that combine chemical properties and protein target properties into a single bioactivity model.
slots.clarification_sentence: This method analyzes both the genetic makeup of the virus and the chemistry of the drugs simultaneously.

slots.claim_sentence: Proteochemometric models performed better than models based only on sequence data in resistance classification.
slots.clarification_sentence: The new approach more accurately predicted how much a virus would resist a specific drug treatment.

slots.claim_sentence: The study identified previously unpublished mutations in HIV Reverse Transcriptase and HIV Protease that confer drug resistance.
slots.clarification_sentence: These specific genetic changes allow the virus to survive even when exposed to standard anti-viral medications.

slots.claim_sentence: The proteochemometric models achieved an 84% correct resistance prediction rate when applied to the public Stanford University HIV resistance database.
slots.clarification_sentence: This high success rate demonstrates the model's ability to handle real-world data from a large patient population.

slots.claim_sentence: The researchers added an applicability domain to the prediction tool to inform users about the reliability of specific predictions.

slots.claim_sentence: Staphylococcus aureus expresses cell wall-anchored proteins to invade host tissues and achieve immune evasion.
slots.clarification_sentence: These specialized proteins allow the bacteria to stick to host cells while hiding from defenses.

slots.claim_sentence: The protein clumping factor B, or ClfB, facilitates Staphylococcus aureus nasal colonization.
slots.clarification_sentence: ClfB helps the bacteria live in the nose by interacting with the cornified envelope.

slots.claim_sentence: Researchers discovered that ClfB is a virulence determinant during Staphylococcus aureus skin infection.
slots.clarification_sentence: This finding shows the protein is a key factor in how the bacteria cause disease.

slots.claim_sentence: ClfB promotes the development of a skin abscess by binding to the host ligand loricrin.
slots.clarification_sentence: Loricrin is a specific protein found in human skin that the bacteria latch onto.

slots.claim_sentence: ClfB influences the abscess structure and bacterial burden within the first 12 hours of infection.
slots.clarification_sentence: The protein is crucial for determining how the infection organizes early in the process.

slots.claim_sentence: A model vaccine targeting ClfB induces protective humoral and cellular immune responses.
slots.clarification_sentence: This vaccine triggers both antibodies and immune cells to defend against the skin infection.

slots.claim_sentence: ClfB is an important candidate antigen for future SSTI vaccines.
slots.clarification_sentence: Targeting this antigen could help prevent difficult-to-treat skin and soft tissue infections.

slots.claim_sentence: Dengue virus causes approximately 100 million symptomatic infections every year.
slots.clarification_sentence: Dengue is a viral infection spread by mosquitoes that affects millions of people globally.

slots.claim_sentence: Dengue infection ranges from mild dengue fever to life-threatening dengue hemorrhagic fever.
slots.clarification_sentence: Dengue fever is abbreviated as DF and dengue hemorrhagic fever as DHF.

slots.claim_sentence: Researchers used mass spectrometry-based metabolomic profiling to analyze the blood sera of patients.
slots.clarification_sentence: Metabolomic profiling is the study of small molecules in the blood called metabolites.

slots.claim_sentence: The study identified 29 metabolites that differed between DF and DHF during the critical phase.
slots.clarification_sentence: The critical phase usually occurs 5 to 7 days after the fever starts.

slots.claim_sentence: Bile acid levels were up to 5 fold higher in DHF patients.
slots.clarification_sentence: These levels correlated with higher levels of liver enzymes AST and ALT indicating liver injury.

slots.claim_sentence: Uric acid levels were 1.5 fold lower in DHF patients compared to DF patients.
slots.clarification_sentence: Uric acid acts as an antioxidant that helps the body protect itself from stress.

slots.claim_sentence: In the recovery phase, eight metabolites remained significantly altered in DHF patients.
slots.clarification_sentence: These altered metabolites included the specific bile acid named chenodeoxyglycocholic acid.

slots.claim_sentence: The identified metabolic pathways provide insights into DHF pathogenesis and suggest possible therapeutic targets.
slots.clarification_sentence: Pathogenesis refers to the process by which the disease develops in the body.

slots.claim_sentence: Cullin-RING ubiquitin ligases must have their substrate receptor subunits tightly controlled to maintain a balanced repertoire of ligases.
slots.clarification_sentence: These ligases are specialized machines that cells use to mark specific proteins for destruction.

slots.claim_sentence: Unbalanced levels of substrate receptors can lead to the sequestration of core components, potentially causing diseases like cancer.
slots.clarification_sentence: This sequestration occurs when a few overabundant receptors hog the core machinery through competition.

slots.claim_sentence: F-box proteins are substrate receptors for the SCF class of ubiquitin ligases.
slots.clarification_sentence: The SCF complex uses these F-box proteins to grab specific targets for degradation.

slots.claim_sentence: Researchers identified a new degradation pathway for the yeast F-box protein Met30 that occurs when it is dissociated from the Skp1 protein.
slots.clarification_sentence: This pathway cleans up Met30 specifically when it is not attached to its usual partner.

slots.claim_sentence: The newly discovered Met30 degradation pathway requires the cullin component Cdc53/Cul1 but is independent of the Skp1 component.
slots.clarification_sentence: This process uses one part of the main machinery while ignoring the part usually required.

slots.claim_sentence: The non-canonical Met30 degradation pathway is essential for maintaining chromosome stability and defending against heavy metal stress.
slots.clarification_sentence: Yeast cells require this system to survive exposure to toxic metals like cadmium.

slots.claim_sentence: The study identifies a functional sub-complex consisting of Cdc53, Rbx1, and Cdc34 that works independently of Skp1 to ubiquitylate Met30.
slots.clarification_sentence: This reveals that parts of the destruction machinery can form a smaller independent team.
